prompting_and_evaluation.name: GitHub Spec Kit
prompting_and_evaluation.relevance: Open-source spec-driven development toolkit from GitHub. Announced 2025-09-02; grew from ~71k★ (Feb 2026) to ~111k★ (Jun 2026) -- treat any star count as stale within weeks and re-check live. Provides structured spec templates, EARS notation integration, and AI-agent-friendly requirements workflows. Docs at https://github.github.com/spec-kit/

prompting_and_evaluation.name: EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax)
prompting_and_evaluation.relevance: Constrained-natural-language requirements notation (When/Where/If/While/The system shall…) developed at Rolls-Royce in 2009, used in spec-driven workflows including GitHub Spec Kit. Reduces ambiguity in acceptance criteria and AI-generated specs.

prompting_and_evaluation.name: Kiro — AWS Spec-Driven AI IDE
prompting_and_evaluation.relevance: AWS spec-driven AI IDE/agent (publicly announced 2025-07-14, GA internationally in 2026) that enforces a spec-first workflow: requirements → design → tasks → implementation. AWS is positioning it as the successor to Amazon Q Developer. Check current docs for pricing, model access, and GA scope -- this category moves faster than any static summary.

prompting_and_evaluation.name: BMAD-METHOD
prompting_and_evaluation.relevance: Open-source agentic spec-driven framework (repo moved from bmadcode/BMAD-METHOD to bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD; update saved links). Structures AI-assisted delivery into Analyst→Architect→Developer→QA agent roles, each consuming specs produced by the previous stage. Reference for multi-agent spec pipeline design.

prompting_and_evaluation.name: Spec-Driven Development: The Spec Is the New Code (@juliandeangeIis)
prompting_and_evaluation.relevance: Community guide on SDD for AI coding — separating functional from technical specs before execution to reduce LLM uncertainty. Covers acceptance criteria, minimal deltas, and using the AI agent's analysis as the spec refinement loop.

measurement_and_research.name: METR: Early-2025 AI and Experienced Open-Source Developers
measurement_and_research.relevance: Useful cautionary reference on measured productivity versus perceived productivity in early-2025 AI tooling. Randomized trial: experienced OSS developers were ~19% slower with early-2025 AI tools on real tasks, yet estimated afterward that AI had made them ~20% faster -- a large perception/measurement gap worth citing whenever a PRD leans on anecdotal "AI made this faster" claims instead of measured evals.

measurement_and_research.name: METR: 2026 productivity experiment update
measurement_and_research.relevance: Important caveat on selection effects and the limits of carrying early-2025 productivity findings forward unchanged.

measurement_and_research.name: Thariq — Using Claude Code: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of HTML
measurement_and_research.relevance: First-party Claude Code team guidance on HTML as default output format for human-facing specs, plans, code reviews, and interactive artifacts. Cited in Output Format section: 100-line read-through threshold, 2-4x generation cost, export-button pattern, design-system HTML reference file.
